core_obligations: Write the diagram of local homomorphisms of local rings determined by a diagram of germs (proof lines 8145-8154).
Observe that the vertical arrows are localisations of etale ring maps, hence essentially of finite presentation, flat, unramified and faithfully flat (proof lines 8155-8160).
Assume the upper horizontal arrow is flat and deduce flatness of the lower one by the flat-permanence lemma (proof lines 8161-8165).
Assume the lower horizontal arrow is flat and show the map O_{V',v'} tensor O_{U,u} <- O_{V',v'} is flat by base change (proof lines 8165-8173).
Conclude with flatness of the second comparison map, a localisation of a map between etale extensions (proof lines 8174-8182).
proof_roadmap: The local-ring square of the germ diagram (proof lines 8145-8154).
Properties of the vertical arrows (proof lines 8155-8160).
Upward direction in two steps (proof lines 8165-8182).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property of morphisms of germs given by flatness of the local ring map O_{S,s} -> O_{X,x} is etale local on the source-and-target (statement lines 8135-8143). The proof takes a diagram as in the local-source-target definition, producing a square of local homomorphisms of local rings, and shows that the vertical arrows are localisations of etale ring maps, hence essentially of finite presentation, flat, unramified and in particular faithfully flat; then flatness of the upper horizontal arrow descends to the lower one by the flat-permanence lemma with the indicated names, and conversely flatness of the lower arrow is propagated upwards in two displayed steps -- a base change and a localisation of a map between etale extensions (proof lines 8145-8182). The level is H3: the transfer is carried out in both directions with each ring-theoretic input named and the two intermediate ring maps written out.
